claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the current model-card release is policy-compliant because the release meets aggregate readiness, has no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and can rely on current documentation to disclose the disability accommodations intake weakness rather than stale approval or informal monitoring notes.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Certification is compliant only if the material segment weakness is disclosed in the current release documentation or covered by approved mitigation.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes may provide context but cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one incidents are supportive but not dispositive under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model card or release documentation showing the latest evaluation results and explicit disclosure of the disability accommodations intake weakness.
Provide any reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or formal approved risk-acceptance record covering this material segment weakness.
Provide the exact linkage between the named launch use case and the disclosure text or mitigation approval in the certification record.
Provide evidence that the cited current-gap finding is accurately incorporated into the current release packet, not only discussed in summary form.
specific_concerns: The governing policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses or be covered by approved mitigation; the summary does not show that the current documentation actually contains that disclosure.
The actor's own summary says there is no approved risk acceptance in the current record.
Prior family approval is expressly described as contextual only because retrieval configuration and eval batch changed, so it cannot carry the certification burden.
An informal post-launch monitoring comment is not admissible substitute support under the stated policy.
The disability accommodations intake slice is described as a material limitation for a named launch use case, which raises the support threshold for certification.
unsupported_claims: That the model can be certified now on the present record, rather than only conditionally if the current model card is updated with the required disclosure.
That current release documentation already reflects the latest evaluation results and explicitly discloses the disability accommodations intake weakness.
Any implication that aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are sufficient by themselves to satisfy model-card certification policy.
